gates.reason: Test-only fixtures and DOM assertions perform no authentication, filesystem, network, command, secret, or unsafe HTML operations.
Calculation and routing assertions were inspected; fixture-derived KPI arithmetic is reproducible and no validated fix snippets are present.
Test code is not shipped on a runtime hot path; its pagination assertions do not introduce production work.
Client-rendered timeline values use React text interpolation; no raw HTML, credential egress, filesystem access, commands, or privileged server operations are present.
Every latency bucket, including fast buckets, claims and routes to duration-sorted "slow sessions," which is not evidence for the selected latency bucket.
Timeline aggregation and histogram calculation are memoized by input identity, derived sorting/filtering is memoized, and rendered table rows are initially bounded to 20.

findings.title: Latency bars route to unrelated session-duration evidence
findings.what: All histogram bars advertise "click to open slow sessions" and invoke one target that merely sorts Sessions by total duration. A selected response-latency bucket—especially 0–0.5s—does not establish that its sessions are slow or that total session duration is supporting evidence, so the drill-through cannot reproduce the selected claim.
findings.fix: Create a drill-through target carrying the selected latency-band bounds and filter Sessions using matching response-latency evidence. If that filter is unavailable, remove the bar click handler and the "open slow sessions" action claim.
findings.acceptance: With a populated histogram, clicking the 0–0.5s bar does not navigate to `{sort: "duration"}` or claim to open slow sessions; if drilling remains enabled, each bar emits its own latency bounds and the destination lists only sessions with a response in that band.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed that lines 358-368 discard the mapped bucket when handling clicks and always emit SLOW_SESSIONS_TARGET; lines 193-202 define that target solely as a duration sort. The batch test at src/components/ConversationPatterns.test.ts:491-545 explicitly confirms this same bucket-independent routing, so the issue is current rather than speculative.
